tools.description: Get the Close user the API key belongs to (own user id, email and the organizations it can reach)

tools.name: list_leads
tools.description: List Close leads (companies) with their status and primary contact details

tools.name: get_lead
tools.description: Get one Close lead by ID, including its contact ids and description

tools.name: list_opportunities
tools.description: List Close opportunities (deals), optionally narrowed to one lead or one status type

status_type.description: Optional status type to filter by (Close uses active, won and lost)

needs_review: Tools added 2026-09-12 from the official Close API reference (https://developer.close.com/llms.txt, the machine index that site publishes): GET /api/v1/me/, GET /api/v1/lead/, GET /api/v1/lead/{id}/ and GET /api/v1/opportunity/. All four are GET reads and every tool carries write:false; lead/opportunity/contact creation and updates exist in the API and are deliberately out of scope this wave.

AUTH UNCHANGED from the scaffold: every endpoint page above documents 'Authorization header (basic auth, required) - Use your API key as the username and leave the password empty', which is exactly the scaffolded basic auth with userField api_key and passField "". Close also accepts a bearer token, but that is the OAuth path and needs a different credential type, so the scaffolded key-in-basic-auth form stands.

The scaffolded test block GET /api/v1/me/ stands: the reference calls it 'a special instance of the Users endpoint for the current user', useful for determining your own id and organization_id, so it proves the key with the smallest possible read.

_limit is clamped to a default of 20 and a maximum of 100 on both list tools. The reference documents _limit default 100 and warns that each resource has its own maximum above which it answers 400, so the clamp keeps the tool inside the documented floor for every resource.

Offset pagination (_skip) is NOT exposed: the reference documents a per-resource maximum _skip it does not publish, and recommends date-range narrowing over deep paging, so a skip input would invite a 400 the tool cannot predict. Both list tools return has_more so a caller can see there is more data.
get_lead returns contact_ids and contacts_summary rather than the lead's embedded contacts array: the reference marks that array deprecated.

Shape-proof 2026-09-12 (proofs/close.proof.json): SHAPE_PROVEN on all 5 probes, each classified on a structured JSON 401 body (flag structured_body: json). api.close.com answers the dummy basic-auth key with 401 {"error": "Unauthorized"} on all four documented paths, and the deterministic control path answers a structurally different 404 ('The requested URL was not found on the server'), so the routes are distinguishable from the auth wall. No 2xx was ever seen: field-level response shapes come from the documentation, not from this run.
